title: Peace between siblings
description: Brothers and sisters keep the longest shared history of our lives; it deserves gentler handling than most of us give it.

body.heading: You are arguing about two different childhoods
paragraphs: Siblings raised in the same house often remember different families: the eldest remembers responsibility, the youngest remembers rules relaxing, everyone remembers being the one who got in trouble. Half of all sibling arguments are really two accurate memories colliding.
Saying “That’s not how it was for me” instead of “That’s not how it was” can lower the temperature of a whole family history.

body.heading: Retire the old roles
paragraphs: Families hand out roles early — the responsible one, the baby, the difficult one — and keep casting them decades later. If you want a better relationship with a sibling, start by refusing the script: ask the “irresponsible” one for advice; let the “strong” one be tired.
People can only change in your company if your company leaves room for the change.

body.heading: Small repairs, made directly
paragraphs: Sibling repairs work best direct and small: not through parents, not at holidays under observation, just a call that says, “That thing last month — I’ve been thinking about it.” The longest relationships of your life are worth a few awkward minutes.
And keep some things sacred: the jokes only you two understand, the shared enemies of childhood, the code words. That archive is an inheritance. Spend effort accordingly.

takeaway: Remember you lived different childhoods, retire the old roles, and repair directly and small.
